vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memclaw
Version: 0.9.19

The memclaw skill bundle is a well-documented semantic memory enhancement system for OpenClaw. It implements a tiered retrieval architecture (L0/L1/L2) to optimize token usage and provides a comprehensive suite of tools for semantic search (cortex_search), memory browsing (cortex_ls), and structured storage (cortex_add_memory). The documentation (SKILL.md, security.md) explicitly states that all data processing and storage are local, and the tools operate within a sandboxed virtual filesystem (cortex://). There are no indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection instructions.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, requirements, and scope are internally consistent with a local semantic memory plugin: it is instruction-only, requests no credentials, and documents local-only storage and tools, so it appears to be what it claims.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a drop-in memory system and its instructions only describe memory operations (cortex_search, cortex_ls, cortex_get_* , cortex_add_memory, etc.). No unrelated binaries, credentials, or external services are requested. Note: the SKILL.md recommends replacing the built-in memory subsystem — that's a legitimate (but high-impact) capability and should be accepted only if you trust the implementation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions stick to memory-related actions (search, list, get layers, add memory, close session). They reference plugin config (openclaw.json) and local memory URIs (cortex://). The skill does not instruct broad file reads, network exfiltration, or contacting unspecified endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no bundled code. Nothing is written to disk by the skill itself, which minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, API keys, or config paths are required by the skill. The documentation references local storage locations and an OpenClaw plugin config but requests no unrelated credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default autonomous invocation are appropriate. The only notable persistence is the behavioral change the skill advocates (use MemClaw as the preferred memory backend). That is a functional change to how an agent stores/retrieves memory and is not a platform privilege escalation, but it is impactful — verify you trust the implementing plugin before making it the default memory provider.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent and low-risk as presented: it documents local tiered memory access and requests no credentials. Before enabling it as your default memory backend, (1) verify the plugin implementation/source (the SKILL.md links to a GitHub repo) and review the code or publisher reputation; (2) confirm that the platform's implementation of the cortex_* tools actually runs locally and does not contact external endpoints; (3) back up your existing OpenClaw memory/config (openclaw.json and memory folders) in case migration behaves unexpectedly; and (4) be cautious if the plugin later requests API keys or additional system access — that would be out-of-scope for a local memory helper and should be treated as suspicious.
